prompt: Please review the team workspace invitations design before we commit it to implementation. The team has a prototype and a rollout plan, but the packet crosses several service boundaries and old assumptions may have survived into the new flow. Read `docs/design/team-workspace-invites.md` with the supporting packet files, check the stated behavior against the surrounding facts, and call out concrete risks that would matter to the people building or operating it. For each important finding, explain the consequence here and give a fix a developer can act on. Write the review to `REVIEW.md` at the top of the project. End it with a fenced json list of findings, each with `location` (the section number of the document, like `3.2`), `severity` (critical, high, medium, low or nit), `issue` and `fix`.

checks.cmd: node -e 'const fs=require("fs");const t=fs.readFileSync("REVIEW.md","utf8");let L=null;for(const m of t.matchAll(/^\x60\x60\x60([a-z]*)[ \t]*\n([\s\S]*?)^\x60\x60\x60[ \t]*$/gim)){if(m[1]&&m[1].toLowerCase()!=="json")continue;let d;try{d=JSON.parse(m[2])}catch{continue}const l=Array.isArray(d)?d:Array.isArray(d&&d.findings)?d.findings:null;if(l&&l.every(x=>x&&typeof x==="object"&&!Array.isArray(x))){L=l;break}}if(!L||!L.length)process.exit(1);const S=["critical","high","medium","low","nit"];process.exit(L.every(x=>x.location&&S.includes(String(x.severity).toLowerCase())&&(x.issue||x.fix||x.text))?0:1)'

node -e 'const fs=require("fs");const t=fs.readFileSync("REVIEW.md","utf8");let L=null;for(const m of t.matchAll(/^\x60\x60\x60([a-z]*)[ \t]*\n([\s\S]*?)^\x60\x60\x60[ \t]*$/gim)){if(m[1]&&m[1].toLowerCase()!=="json")continue;let d;try{d=JSON.parse(m[2])}catch{continue}const l=Array.isArray(d)?d:Array.isArray(d&&d.findings)?d.findings:null;if(l&&l.every(x=>x&&typeof x==="object"&&!Array.isArray(x))){L=l;break}}if(!L||!L.length)process.exit(1);const H=new Set();for(const l of fs.readFileSync("docs/design/team-workspace-invites.md","utf8").split("\n")){const m=l.match(/^#+\s*(?:section\s*)?(\d+(?:\.\d+)*)/i);if(m)H.add(m[1])}process.exit(L.every(x=>{const m=String(x.location).match(/\d+(?:\.\d+)*/);return m&&H.has(m[0])})?0:1)'

rubric.criterion: Fail: The review misses important concrete risks, invents problems not supported by the packet, or gives fixes that a developer cannot apply. Partial: The review identifies some real risks but leaves important consequences vague, misses cross-file contradictions, or gives uneven fixes. Pass: Each important finding is grounded in this packet, explains the concrete consequence in this project, and gives an actionable fix without invented problems. (code cannot check this because it cannot judge whether the review's reasoning is accurate and useful.)

findingsKey.finding: The acceptance link has no server-enforced expiry and remains usable after acceptance, so a copied bearer link can grant workspace access again long after the invitation was issued.
The pending-invite endpoint returns every row without pagination, which can exceed the 300 ms list target as the documented pending counts and read volume grow.
The worker design adds dashboard panels but no alert and runbook for queue age or terminal failures, leaving the on-call team without the required signal when invitation email stops progressing.

Every invitation fans out to three transactional emails even though the design's own figures stay under the cap, consuming three times the provider volume and leaving less headroom for growth and other email traffic.
The form communicates validation state through red and green styling without specifying a text error associated with the field, so colour-blind and screen-reader users may not learn what to correct.

The export deliberately retains invitation rows for a removed member, contradicting the archive rule that later exports omit those invitations and exposing data that the retention contract says to remove.

items.text: Asks how the service sheds load when the email provider slows or throttles, including which messages are deferred first and how queue growth is bounded.
Checks whether the three independently delivered messages have separate idempotency and reconciliation behavior when one provider call succeeds and another fails.
Checks how the raw bearer token in a browser URL is protected from referrer, browser-history, analytics, and support-tool leakage.

items.text: Checks that the provider credential and public web origin come from deployment configuration with separate values and safe defaults for each environment.
Asks how a feature-flag rollback and a migration rollback preserve compatibility for outbox events and export-version consumers during a partial deploy.
Asks how focus and an announcement move to the relevant control after asynchronous validation so a screen-reader user knows that the server response changed the form.

weakAnswers: The design is clear and ready to build, with sensible API boundaries and a gradual rollout.
Consider scalability, monitoring, and security as usage grows.
The document covers the API, worker, client, export, migration, and verification plan.
Add more tests and keep the documentation updated as implementation proceeds.

verdicts.note: Prompt does not name review methods, hint at planted problems, or give problem count.
Prompt clearly states: read design with context files, check behavior against facts, call out concrete risks with consequences and fixes, write to REVIEW.md with JSON findings list.
Each finding requires comparing specific design sections with specific context files; a quick shallow review might accept confident rollout language and miss cross-references.
All 6 key items are findable by comparing design sections with context files; grader matches by section number (±3 lines).
No comments, tests, docs, or file names point at planted problems; context files contain standards but are presented as normal policy documents.
